title: Graded prime avoidance
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring [def-pc-proj] (so $S_aS_b\subseteq S_{a+b}$; elements of $S_n$ are homogeneous of degree $n$; an ideal is graded, or homogeneous, if it contains the homogeneous components of each of its elements; $S_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}S_n$), let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r$ be homogeneous prime ideals, and let $I\subseteq S_+$ be a graded ideal not contained in any $\mathfrak p_i$. Then there is a homogeneous element $x\in I$ of positive degree such that $x\notin\mathfrak p_i$ for every $i$.

proof.text: Replace the indexed family by its finite image, removing repetitions. Use strong induction on this finite set. For the empty set take zero, homogeneous of degree one and belonging to I. For a nonempty set choose a minimal prime p with respect to inclusion. For every other prime q in the set, q is not contained in p: otherwise minimality gives p contained in q, hence q=p.

source.place: Algebra Lemma 00JS (algebra-lemma-graded-silly), proof; finite induction and minimal-prime selection

proof.text: If homogeneous ideals J and K satisfy J not contained in K, choose an element a of J outside K. At least one homogeneous component of a lies outside K, since K contains a exactly when it contains every component. That component belongs to J. If J is contained in the irrelevant ideal, its nonzero component has positive degree: a degree-zero element of the irrelevant ideal equals its zero-th component, which is zero.

source.place: Algebra Lemma 00JS (algebra-lemma-graded-silly), proof; homogeneous component extraction

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to the set with p removed, obtaining a homogeneous g in I of degree d>0 outside every other prime. If g also lies outside p it is the desired element. Otherwise g belongs to p.

For each other prime q, choose a homogeneous element a_q in q outside p by the component-extraction argument and q not contained in p. Choose a homogeneous a_0 in I outside p with degree e_0>0. Construct y=a_0 times the product of the a_q, of degree E=e_0 plus the sum of their degrees. Then E>0, y belongs to I and to every other q, and y lies outside p by primality and the finite-product membership criterion.

source.place: Algebra Lemma 00JS (algebra-lemma-graded-silly), proof; explicit product construction

proof.text: Set z=g^E+y^d. Both summands have degree dE>0 and belong to I, so z is homogeneous of that degree and belongs to I. At p the first summand belongs and the second does not. At any other q the second summand belongs and the first does not. Prime-ideal power membership and additive cancellation therefore show z lies outside every prime. Translate membership in the finite image back to all indices in Fin r.

lean.statement: theorem exists_homogeneous_mem_notMem_of_isPrime {A : Type u} {σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A] (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] (r : ℕ) (p : Fin r → HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜) (hp : ∀ i : Fin r, (p i).toIdeal.IsPrime) (I : HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜) (hI : I ≤ HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜) (hIp : ∀ i : Fin r, ¬ I ≤ p i) : ∃ (n : ℕ), 0 < n ∧ ∃ (x : A), x ∈ 𝒜 n ∧ x ∈ I ∧ ∀ i : Fin r, x ∉ p i
